fullPassage:
(A) The manager of the Humane Society was out of town for two weeks, and Elaine was placed in charge. Since she had taken on this responsibility before, she was familiar with the challenges she might encounter — impounding stray animals, reuniting pets with their owners, informing people their pet hadn't been found, accepting animals from those who could no longer care for them, or turning animals away when the shelter was full. Though she found the work demanding, (a) she handled these situations with confidence and calm.

(B) Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager, who encouraged her to let it all out. Elaine shared what happened and released (b) her emotions while the manager listened. She felt much better afterward and was relieved to have someone she could talk to without fear of judgment. Since then, the manager has encouraged staff to come to her if they need to release emotions kept in at work — and she listens.

(C) Elaine calmly explained that there was no space available, but the woman became visibly upset and said, "If you don't take this cat, I'll just have to let it go somewhere." Although such statements were sadly not unusual, they always troubled Elaine. Still, (c) she maintained professionalism, offered contact information for other shelters, and tried to help. The woman complained the alternatives were too far and repeated she had no other choice. Elaine then suggested the shelter might find a volunteer to transport the cat. In response, the woman, showing her frustration toward (d) her, placed the cat's kennel in front of her, raised her voice, and left the shelter.

(D) On the first day of the manager's absence, everything was running smoothly until a woman arrived with a cat and asked to leave it at the shelter. Elaine's first question was whether the cat was a stray or not, since the shelter was obligated to take in strays but could refuse owned pets. The woman said it was her cat and explained that she was moving and couldn't take it with (e) her — a common excuse. Although the shelter sometimes accepted pets in such cases, it was already housing over ninety cats, nearly double its capacity of fifty, so Elaine had to politely refuse.

questions.passage:
The manager of the Humane Society was out of town for two weeks, and Elaine was placed in (A)[charge / danger]. Since she had taken on this (B)[responsibility / vacation] before, she was (C)[familiar / unfamiliar] with the challenges she might encounter. Though she found the work demanding, (a) she handled these situations with confidence and calm.

(B) Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager, who encouraged her to let it all out. Elaine shared what happened and released (b) her emotions while the manager listened.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Elaine은 책임(charge)을 맡았고, 이 책무(responsibility)를 이전에 맡은 적이 있어 도전들에 익숙했습니다(familiar).
det.analysis:
✅ ① charge — responsibility — familiar: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② danger(위험): 책임을 맡은 것이지 위험에 처한 것이 아님
❌ ③ vacation(휴가): 책무이지 휴가가 아님
❌ ④ unfamiliar(낯선): 이전에 경험했으므로 familiar
det.tip: placed in charge(책임을 맡다), take on responsibility(책무를 떠맡다), familiar with(~에 익숙한)

questions.passage: Elaine shared what happened and released (b) her emotions while the manager listened. She felt much better afterward and was relieved to have someone she could talk to without fear of judgment. Elaine calmly explained that there was no space (A)[available / occupied], but the woman became visibly (B)[upset / relieved]. Although such statements were sadly not (C)[unusual / surprising], they always troubled Elaine. The woman complained the alternatives were too far and repeated she had no other choice. Elaine then suggested the shelter might find a volunteer to transport the cat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이용 가능한(available) 공간이 없었고, 여자는 눈에 띄게 화가 났으며(upset), 그런 말들은 슬프게도 드문 일이 아니었습니다(not unusual).
det.analysis:
✅ ① available — upset — unusual: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② occupied(점유된): available과 반대 의미로 맥락 불일치
❌ ③ relieved(안도한): upset의 반의어
❌ ④ surprising: unusual과 유사하나 원문은 unusual
det.tip: not unusual = 드문 일이 아닌(이중부정). 반복되는 상황이라는 맥락

questions.passage: Since she had taken on this responsibility before, she was familiar with the challenges she might encounter — impounding stray animals, reuniting pets with their owners, informing people their pet hadn't been found, accepting animals from those who could no longer care for them, or turning animals away when the shelter was full. Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back (A)[isolation / exhibition] area. det.korean: 뒷쪽 격리(isolation) 구역에 고양이를 데려가고, 매니저는 감정을 내보내도록 격려(encouraged)했으며, Elaine이 감정을 풀어놓는 동안 매니저는 경청했습니다(listened).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ isolation — encouraged — listened: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ① exhibition(전시): isolation(격리)의 반대 맥락
❌ ② discouraged(만류): encouraged(격려)의 반의어
❌ ④ interrupted(가로막다): listened(경청)의 반대
det.tip: isolation(격리), encouraged(격려), listened(경청) — 감정 지원의 핵심 어휘

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④chaotically(혼란스럽게)는 원문의 smoothly(순조롭게)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ chaotically(혼란스럽게) → smoothly(순조롭게): 여자가 오기 전까지는 순조로웠음
det.tip: smoothly(순조롭게) ↔ chaotically(혼란스럽게): until이 전환점

questions.passage: The woman said it was her cat and explained that she was ①<u>moving</u> and couldn't take it with her — a ②<u>common</u> excuse. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④accept(수락하다)는 원문의 refuse(거절하다)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ accept(수락) → refuse(거절): 정원의 두 배이므로 거절해야 하는 상황
det.tip: accept(수락) ↔ refuse(거절): 정원 초과 상황에서 거절이 적절

questions.passage: Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④praise(칭찬)는 원문의 judgment(판단)를 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ praise(칭찬) → judgment(판단): '칭찬에 대한 두려움'이 아닌 '판단에 대한 두려움' 없이 이야기할 수 있는 상대
det.tip: without fear of judgment(판단에 대한 두려움 없이): 감정을 솔직히 표현할 수 있는 안전한 관계

❌ ① rewards(보상): 힘든 상황들을 나열하므로 부적절
❌ ③ celebrations(축하): 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ promotions(승진): 업무 내용과 무관
det.tip: challenges = 어려움, 도전. 뒤에 나열되는 내용이 모두 힘든 업무

det.korean: 보호소는 유기동물을 받아들일 의무가 있었습니다(obligated).
det.analysis:
✅ ① obligated(의무가 있는): 유기동물 vs 소유 반려동물의 법적 의무 차이
❌ ② reluctant(꺼리는): 의무와 다른 의미
❌ ③ forbidden(금지된): 받아들여야 하므로 반대
❌ ④ eager(열망하는): 의무이지 열망이 아님
det.tip: obligated to = ~할 의무가 있는. 법적 의무(stray) vs 선택(owned pet)

det.korean: Elaine은 판단(judgment)에 대한 두려움 없이 이야기할 수 있는 사람이 있어 안도했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ judgment(판단): 감정 표현에 대한 판단 없이 들어주는 관계
❌ ① failure(실패): 감정 표현과 직접 관련 없음

❌ ③ punishment(처벌): 감정 표현이 처벌받는 맥락이 아님
det.tip: without fear of judgment = 판단에 대한 두려움 없이. 심리적 안전감의 핵심

questions.passage: Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel. Then she called the <u>absent</u> manager, who encouraged her to let it all out.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 absent와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: absent는 '부재중인'이라는 뜻으로, present(출석한)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ present(출석한) ↔ absent(부재중인)
❌ ① missing(없는): absent와 유사
❌ ② unavailable(이용 불가): absent와 유사

questions.passage:
(A) The manager of the Humane Society was out of town, and Elaine was placed in <u>charge</u>.

(B) There is no extra <u>charge</u> for delivering the pet food to your home.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 charge가 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A)에서 placed in charge는 책임을 맡다, (B)에서 no extra charge는 추가 요금이 없다는 뜻입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 책임 — (B) 요금: 각 문맥에 정확히 부합
❌ ① (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③④ 비난/충전은 두 문맥 모두 부적절
det.tip: charge: 책임(in charge)/요금(no charge)/비난(charge with)/충전(charge a battery) — 대표적 다의어

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"a domestic animal that has been lost or abandoned and wanders without an owner"

✅ ① stray(유기동물): 영영풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ② pet(반려동물): 주인이 있는 동물
❌ ③ volunteer(자원봉사자): 사람
❌ ④ shelter(보호소): 장소

questions.passage: Elaine calmly explained that there was no space available. Still, she maintained __________ (profession), offered contact information for other shelters, and tried to help.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: profession(직업) → professionalism(전문성). 동사 maintained의 목적어로 명사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
maintained + __________ 구조에서 동사의 목적어 → 명사 필요 → professionalism
profession(명) → professional(형) → professionalism(명: 전문성)
det.tip: profession(직업) → professional(전문적인) → professionalism(전문성): -ism 접미사는 추상 명사

questions.passage: Since she had taken on this responsibility before, she was familiar with the challenges she might encounter. Though she found the work demanding, she handled these situations with __________ (confident) and calm.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: confident(형용사: 자신감 있는) → confidence(명사: 자신감). 전치사 with 뒤에 명사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
with + __________ + and calm 구조에서 전치사 뒤 명사 필요 → confidence
confident(형) → confidence(명) → confidently(부)
det.tip: confident(자신감 있는, 형) → confidence(자신감, 명): -ence 접미사는 명사화
